proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By the definition of the floor function, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Therefore floor(x) itself is an integer satisfying floor(x) ≤ x. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x.
solver_summary: Directly from the definition of the floor function as the greatest integer not exceeding its argument, floor(x) is always at most x.
vetter_reason: The proof correctly restates the definition of floor(x) as the greatest integer less than or equal to x, from which floor(x) ≤ x follows immediately. The argument is universal in x and matches the lemma exactly.
